clue.text: Figure of speech used around university group

indicators.note: the figure of speech is placed around the university letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a trope is a figure of speech, such as a metaphor

explanation.surface: A rhetorical device in use at some university society.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of performers, a group travelling and working together.

clue.text: Like some players, strain on pitch

parts.note: a strain is a kind or variety, a type
to pitch is to throw, to cast

explanation.surface: Footballers, perhaps, suffering a muscle strain on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' and 'pitch' look like sport injury and field; they are the nouns type and the verb cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors repeatedly given the same kind of role are said to be typecast.

clue.text: Sash round one that can go either way

parts.note: O is round in shape

parts.words: one that can go either way
parts.note: bi is informal for bisexual, someone attracted either way

explanation.surface: A reversible sash worn around the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash tied around a Japanese kimono.

clue.text: Eat sparingly with a company in part of a muster?

indicators.note: the article and the company go in the middle of the word for eating sparingly

parts.note: to peck at food is to eat only a little

explanation.surface: Soldiers on a short-rations muster eat sparingly with their company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muster' suggests a military parade, but it is the collective noun for a group of these birds; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A muster is the collective term for a gathering of peafowl, so one bird is a member of it.

clue.text: Airport said to allow Poles entry

indicators.note: the word for said lets the poles in, so they sit inside it
entry confirms the poles go into the middle of the other word

parts.note: said means stated
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: An airport is reportedly letting Polish travellers in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' tempts a homophone, but it just means STATED. 'Poles' are not people from Poland but the compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Stansted is one of the main airports serving London, in Essex.

clue.text: Book — avoiding parking — trips on electric cars — useful!

indicators.note: the word trips avoids, leaves out, the parking letter

parts.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
trams are electric streetcars
handy means useful

explanation.surface: A reader who avoids parking finds trips by electric tram handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes P from TRIPS, leaving TRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristram Shandy is Laurence Sterne's eighteenth-century comic novel.

clue.text: What's hard in writing down cipher

indicators.note: the hard letter sits in the middle of the word for writing down

parts.note: noting is writing down
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking what is difficult when writing down a code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cipher' looks like a code, but here it is its older sense of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is the figure zero, and so a nonentity or nought.

clue.text: Not giving much out, like Spooner's torch?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two parts exchange their first letters

parts.note: a torch is a stick with a light at its tip, so light-tipped
taken with torch, like a torch means tipped with flame

explanation.surface: A secretive person compared with a torch in Spooner's muddled words.
explanation.walkthrough: A torch is light-tipped; swap the opening letters L and T of the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reticent keeps their mouth shut and gives away little information.

clue.text: Strip, getting half nudged into river

indicators.note: the half word is put into the middle of the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

indicators.note: half means only the first three of the six letters of nudged are used

explanation.surface: Someone stripping off after being half pushed into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to lay bare, removing a covering.

clue.text: Cooking up eats with a grannie in her eighth decade?

indicators.note: cooking up the letters means concocting them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grandmother in her seventies cooking a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' signals the anagram of UP EATS A GRANNIE; the grannie in the fodder is also the person defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged in their seventies has completed seven decades and is living through the eighth.

clue.text: A little ship going round, one holding mail items?

indicators.note: the letters go round and round, so they are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small vessel circling with a sailor holding the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail items' are stamps, which this collector holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp collector keeps and holds postage stamps, which are items of mail.

clue.text: Soldier gaining new spirit

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier picking up fresh morale.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin is a juniper-flavoured distilled liquor, a spirit.

clue.text: Company marks appointment that will stimulate growth

parts.note: M stands for marks, the old German currency
a post is a job or appointment

explanation.surface: A firm marks a new hire that should boost business.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotted organic matter is dug into soil as a fertiliser to help plants grow.

clue.text: Noble big cat has walk displacing start of lunch

indicators.note: the walk takes the place of the opening letter of lunch in the big cat

parts.note: a lioness is a female big cat

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of lunch

parts.note: to march is to walk briskly

explanation.walkthrough: 'displacing start of lunch' swaps the L of LIONESS for MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchioness is a woman of noble rank, the wife of a marquess.

clue.text: It isn't a newspaperman that's corrupt

parts.note: 'taint is a dialect contraction of it ain't, meaning it isn't
ED is short for editor, a newspaperman

explanation.surface: A denial that a journalist is the corrupt one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tainted means contaminated or morally corrupted.

clue.text: Arbiter asking a criminal to agree on terms

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked, so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge being asked by a crook to settle.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to a deal over price or conditions is idiomatically to conclude one.

clue.text: Drunken larks in a far country

indicators.note: the letters stagger drunkenly into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drunken pranks abroad in some distant land.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is an island nation off southern India, far from Britain.

clue.text: Fish given to one with cat, perhaps an impish young one?

indicators.note: the fish is given to, placed after, the person with the cat

parts.note: the cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, so its user is a flogger
a snapper is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Feeding a fish to a cat owner's mischievous child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' is not a pet but the cat-o'-nine-tails whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky, presumptuous youngster is called this, an informal term for a brat.

clue.text: Vision of men abandoning parentless cat

indicators.note: the men abandon, are taken out of, the word for parentless

parts.note: an orphan has no parents
OR are other ranks, ordinary soldiers or men
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A ghostly image of men deserting a stray cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes OR from ORPHAN, leaving PHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparition or ghostly figure seen is a vision.

clue.text: Get carving in a cathedral in grave style

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
get carving is an instruction to cut

explanation.surface: An instruction to start carving gravestones in a cathedral.

clue.text: Stick plug at this point

explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface.

clue.text: Model set to portray one of Zeus's lovers in play?

parts.note: a drama is a play

explanation.surface: A stage set built to depict a myth about Zeus.

clue.text: Rue land being redeveloped in Sussex town

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Regretting land being built on in a Sussex town.
explanation.definitionFit: Arundel is a town in West Sussex, England, known for its castle.

clue.text: Before the Revolution devours it

indicators.note: the words the Revolution swallow the answer, holding it inside them

explanation.surface: A historic time before the Revolution swallowed everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere is an archaic word for prior to.

clue.text: Another like Eva and Juan possessing son like theirs

definitions.note: grammatical category of pronouns such as they and them

parts.note: a third is another one after Eva and Juan

indicators.note: the Peron couple possess, hold, the son inside their name

parts.note: Eva and Juan Peron were Argentina's first lady and president

explanation.surface: A third Argentinian like the Perons, with a son of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' works because Eva and Juan make two of a kind; the definition plays on 'theirs' as a pronoun, not on the couple's possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like they, them and their are pronouns in the grammatical category referring to others.

clue.text: Turned irrational after small drink

indicators.note: the turned piece comes after the small letter
turned means the irrational number is written backwards

parts.note: pi is an irrational number

explanation.surface: Someone who went crazy after a small drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' is not mad but the irrational number pi.
explanation.definitionFit: A sip is a small mouthful of a drink.

clue.text: European window destroys Conservative peace

clue.text: Lack of foresight in my work leads to inadequate assessment
